newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell to adopt human rights as business principle.
newsitem.headline: Shell to adopt human rights as business principle.

text.p: Oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday it is to review its business principles and will likely focus on human rights.

"We're currently reviewing our business principles statement and are looking positively at including an explicit reference to human rights," spokesman Bert Regeer said, adding the revised statement should be ready by the year-end.

Shell's comments came in response to an earlier joint statement from two human rights groups -- Dutch Christian group Pax Christi and Amnesty International -- which met a Shell delegation in Rotterdam last week.
"Shell has said it will voice its support for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in its Statement of General Business Principles," the statement said.
Shell has faced a barrage of criticism in the last 18 months for its Nigerian operations and its planned deep-sea disposal of the Brent Spar oil platform.
"The (PaxChristi/Amnesty) statement provides a fair reflection of the meeting, although there are a number of points of detail we will need to talk (over) further," Regeer said.
Shell plans to meet Pax Christi and Amnesty again before then and to continue discussions with other pressure groups.
The two groups said Shell would also declare that "it is legitimate for (Shell) to speak out against serious violations of human rights".
"(Its) principle of political non-interference will be redefined," the statement said.
Shell has previously said that it could make political decisions, but had neither the power nor responsibility to influence the political activities of the countries in which it operates.
Amnesty/Pax Christi said they asked Shell whether it intended to make representations to the Nigerian government over the detention of oil trade union leaders.
Shell was embroiled in controversy when writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other MOSOP (Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples) activists were executed last November.
Shell operates in Nigeria, but pulled out of Ogoniland in 1993 following sabotage of its installations by MOSOP.
